source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: Timer
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a scheduled one-shot callback created by `createTimer(callbackFn, fireDate, reference, context)`, addressable and cancellable by its `reference` (typically `meta.id`); the core scheduling primitive across this whole batch of pages

concepts.label: Timer callback
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the JavaScript function (e.g. `DocTimerCallback`) invoked with the stored `context` when a Timer fires

concepts.label: Control document
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a document whose mutation is used purely as an out-of-band signal (boolean flags like `needed_condition`, `cancel_timer`, `overwrite_timer`) to tell an OnUpdate handler whether to create, cancel, or overwrite a Timer, rather than representing business data itself

relations.subject: eventing:on-update-handler
relations.evidence: The Timer callback function relies on a control document which, if mutated, controls whether a Timer is created, cancelled, or overwritten.

relations.subject: eventing:control-document
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - verb phrase for a control-document mutation causing a new Timer to be scheduled
relations.evidence: If `needed_condition` is true but both `cancel_timer` and `overwrite_timer` are false, the Eventing Function creates a Timer that fires 60 seconds into the future.

relations.subject: eventing:control-document
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - verb phrase for a control-document mutation causing an existing Timer to be cancelled by matching reference
relations.evidence: If both `needed_condition` and `cancel_timer` are true, the Eventing Function cancels the existing Timer.

relations.subject: eventing:control-document
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - verb phrase for the overwrite case, which is explicitly documented as cancel-then-recreate under the identical reference rather than a distinct atomic 'overwrite' primitive
relations.evidence: This is similar to cancelling a Timer that already exists, and then creating a new Timer that fires 60 seconds after it has been overwritten.

relations.subject: eventing:timer
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - verb phrase for the fire-time invocation relationship between a Timer and its callback function
relations.evidence: When a Timer created by the Eventing Function fires, the callback `DocTimerCallback` executes and writes a new document in the target collection with the same key as the document in the source collection.

relations.subject: eventing:on-update-handler
relations.evidence: If both `cancel_timer` and `overwrite_timer` are true, the Eventing Function throws an error and nothing happens.

relations.subject: eventing:eventing-storage
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - minted in eventing-example-data-enrichment.json; recurs verbatim on this page
relations.evidence: Do not add, modify, or delete documents in the Eventing storage keyspace `rr100.eventing.metadata` while your Eventing Functions are in a deployed state.

notable_absence.finding: The mutually-exclusive cancel/overwrite conditions are enforced entirely by hand-written if/else branching in the sample JavaScript (four explicit boolean-combination branches) - there is no dedicated Eventing API or settings-page control for 'timer conflict resolution'; the control-document pattern is a documentation convention, not a platform feature with its own name.
